RFC7606-5.1-1.note: {gap} is honest and confirmed: buildUpdatePayload (wireu/split.go:440-476) writes the attribute section as baseAttrs, then mpUnreach, then mpReach (:463-470), so MP_REACH is emitted LAST, not 'the very first path attribute' as §5.1 SHALL requires. Disclosed in docs/architecture/wire/mp-nlri-ordering.md ('MP_REACH last: Intentionally non-compliant') and rfc-status.md gap (1).

RFC7606-5.1-2.note: {gap} confirmed: buildUpdatePayload (wireu/split.go:440) fills ipv4Withdraws + mpUnreach + mpReach + ipv4NLRI into one payload, and the slow-path loop split.go:209-283 fills all four NLRI-bearing categories per emitted UPDATE (:281). split_test.go:1014 (TestBuildUpdatePayload_Mixed) builds a payload with BOTH non-empty Withdrawn Routes and non-empty NLRI, violating the MUST NOT. CAVEAT/UNSURE: rfc-status.md gap (1) only discloses the §5.1 *ordering* half ('MP_UNREACH first, MP_REACH last'); the 'more than one NLRI-bearing field' violation is not spelled out in the public row, so this specific gap is under-disclosed there even though the rfc/short annotation is detailed.

RFC7606-5.1-3.note: {single-polarity} positive is honest: a MUST-accept obligation has no conforming rejection. rfc7606_test.go:583 (TestRFC7606MPReachIPv4NextHopValid) places MP_REACH after ORIGIN and AS_PATH (not first) and asserts ActionNone. Ze has no receive-side ordering check, so it accepts any position; if an ordering check were added that rejected non-first MP, this would fail. Caveat: proves the 'any position' clause but not the 'combination' clause.

RFC7606-5.2-1.note: Negatives pin the escalation exactly: rfc7606_test.go:1328 (malformed ORIGIN len=2) and :2142 (ORIGIN len=5) both assert require.Equal(SessionReset) + Contains('5.2'), driving rfc7606.go:336-342 (!hasNLRI && mpReachCount==0 && strongest>AttributeDiscard). Positives pin both exemptions: :1348/:2155 assert attribute-discard-only stays AttributeDiscard (NOT escalated), and :1308 (MP_UNREACH-only, no NLRI, no error) asserts ActionNone. The 'other than MP_UNREACH' EoR clause is only exercised in its no-error form.

RFC7606-5.3-1.note: Negative session_validate_test.go:107 (TestEnforceRFC7606_InvalidTrailingNLRI) runs the production path enforceRFC7606 -> ValidateNLRISyntax(nlri,false) on a trailing /33; asserts require.Error + require.Equal(SessionReset). RFC7606-5.3-2.note: negative (session_validate_test.go TestEnforceRFC7606_InvalidWithdrawnNLRI) now uses a /24 Withdrawn NLRI with only 2 octets present (24<=32, so the >32 rule 5.3-1 cannot fire); enforceRFC7606 -> ValidateNLRISyntax on the Withdrawn field (session_validation.go:54) returns SessionReset via the overrun clause. RFC7606-5.3-3.note: MP NLRI length-vs-AFI/SAFI is enforced by validateMPNLRIField in the ValidateUpdateRFC7606 main loop (ADD-PATH aware: skips the RFC 7911 4-byte path id) -> ValidateNLRISyntaxAddPath. RFC7606-5.3-6.note: Positive structural_test.go:163 (TestRFC7606MPMinimumLengthsAccepted) pins the exact minimums: MP_REACH len 5 -> ActionNone and MP_UNREACH len 3 -> ActionNone, so an off-by-one that rejected the minimum (e.g. '<6') fails here. Caveat: the len=2 negative does not isolate the '<5' boundary (a 2-byte MP_REACH also fails next-hop parse), so an implementation accepting len=4 might slip through; but the positive discriminates the accepting side and the end-to-end reset+NOTIFICATION is proven.

RFC7606-5.4-1.note: {gap} confirmed: ParseEVPN (component/bgp/plugins/nlri/evpn/types.go:237-244) maps reserved/unknown route types (0,6-15 and any unmatched) to EVPNGeneric, which has a working WriteTo, so unrecognized typed NLRI is RETAINED and re-advertised, not discarded. ParseMVPN (component/bgp/plugins/nlri/mvpn/types.go:113-146) reads routeType (:118) but never branches on it, always returning a valid *MVPN. Both violate §5.4's MUST-discard. Disclosed in rfc-status.md gap (2).

RFC7606-6-1.note: {gap} confirmed: the RFC 7606 log sites log attr code + description only, no NLRI listing and no malformed UPDATE bytes, though body/wu are in scope: attribute-discard session_validation.go:110-113, treat-as-withdraw :148-150, session-reset :178. §6's minimum (log NLRI + entire malformed UPDATE) is not met. Disclosed in rfc-status.md gap (7). (Worksheet correctly flags §6 uses lowercase 'must', kept at MUST as a Ze policy choice, not an RFC 2119 keyword.)

RFC7606-7.13-1.note: Honest {gap}. Attribute code 24 (Traffic Engineering, RFC 5543) has no RFC 7606 validator: attrValidators (rfc7606.go:363-379) registers only codes 1-10,14,15,16,32,40, and validateAttribute returns nil for any unregistered code (rfc7606.go:382-387), so a malformed TE attribute of any length is accepted where §7.13 mandates treat-as-withdraw. Annotation accurately describes the code.

RFC7606-7.14-1.note: Positive rfc7606_test.go:187 (len-8 Extended Community) asserts ActionNone; negative rfc7606_test.go:218 (len-0) asserts exact TreatAsWithdraw + AttrCode 16 + "7.14", isolated as the last attribute with no trailing bytes (comment 212-215). Note: only the zero-length ('non-zero') clause is tagged; the 'not a multiple of 8' clause for nonzero lengths (e.g. 12) is untagged, so dropping the `length%8!=0` check while keeping `==0` in validateExtCommunityAttr (rfc7606.go:551) would pass the tagged tests. The code implements both clauses.

RFC7606-7.14-2.note: Single-polarity (positive-only) argument holds: §7.14 is a MUST NOT prohibition ('MUST NOT treat an unrecognized Extended Community Type or Sub-Type as an error'), so acceptance is the only conforming observation. Positive rfc7606_test.go:247 uses valid length 8 with unrecognized Type 0x3f/Sub-Type 0xee and asserts ActionNone; length kept valid so the 7.14-1 length clause cannot mask the type question. validateExtCommunityAttr (rfc7606.go:550-560) inspects only length, never type, so introducing a type allowlist would flip this test to TreatAsWithdraw and fail it.

RFC7606-7.15-1.note: Honest {gap}. Attribute code 25 (IPv6 Address Specific Extended Community) is declared in attribute.go:62 but has no validator in attrValidators (rfc7606.go:363-379), so validateAttribute returns nil (:382-387); a zero-length or non-multiple-of-20 IPv6 extended community is silently accepted where §7.15 mandates treat-as-withdraw. Annotation accurate.

RFC7606-7.15-2.note: Honest {gap}, though the MUST NOT is technically satisfied by omission: code 25 is entirely unvalidated (attrValidators rfc7606.go:363-379), so an unrecognized IPv6 ext-community Type/Sub-Type is never treated as an error, but by absence of code rather than by design, and no test can pin behaviour no code produces. Annotation is honest about this. (Least-certain id: an alternative reading is 'vacuously satisfied' rather than unimplemented, but the code lacks any deliberate handling of code 25.)

RFC7606-7.16-1.note: Honest {gap}. A malformed ATTR_SET is therefore accepted where §7.16 mandates treat-as-withdraw. Annotation accurately describes both facts.

RFC7606-8-1.note: {not-applicable} annotation holds up: RFC §8 ('A document that specifies a new BGP attribute MUST provide specifics regarding what constitutes an error...') binds AUTHORS of future BGP attribute specifications, not a running implementation. There is genuinely no Ze code path that could satisfy or violate it, so it is not implementable (per the method, an implementable N/A would be 'wrong' -- this one is not). Recorded 'enforced' only in the sense that the N/A classification is honest and correct; there is no test to demand and no finding.
